A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, diagrams, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original numerical degree computations. Example D.1 also reports observed computational behavior: two formulations failed to terminate within a reasonable time, while factorization returned the degree immediately.

after.justification: The original numerical degree computations and the computational comparison in Example D.1 are retained.

M1.justification: The balancedness checks, Jacobian tests, stabilizer reduction, factorization and degree-computation procedures are retained. Appendix E applies the existing normalization approach in a new classification proof, without introducing a distinct algorithm.

E1.justification: The computationally investigated multi-view configurations and worked computational examples are unchanged. The added single-view configurations are established analytically, rather than evaluated in a new experiment.

E2.justification: Example D.1 retains the comparison with naive equations and elimination of world-line variables. The additional citations do not introduce newly evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Both versions describe finite-field Jacobian checks on 434 candidate problems, monodromy degree computations and symbolic verification for problems with up to four views. Added code locations do not revise these settings.

E4.justification: The factorization examples in Section 4.12 and Appendix D, including their computational observations, are retained. Appendix E adds formal classification results, without adding ablations, robustness tests or empirical supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions describe repeating Jacobian checks at several random points. Neither adds exact repetition counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or other statistical reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports eight base single-view configurations, all of degree 1, with five allowing arbitrarily many dependent points. These are analytical results. The existing multi-view configurations and degrees match throughout v1 Tables 7–10 and v2 Tables 9–12.

T1.justification: New Appendix E supplies a single-camera classification through Proposition E.1, Lemmas E.2–E.3, a dimension equation and constructive normalizations. Theorem 2.3 and Lemmas 4.1 and A.1 now explicitly require at least two views, replacing v1's blanket assertion that minimal problems require multiple cameras.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: 291 multi-view minimal problems, 73 with unique solutions, and stabilizer-based non-minimality certificates and factorization. The additional single-view theory does not change these headline claims.

C2.justification: Remark E.4 adds an applicability explanation: the two arbitrary-view families permit independent camera registration in a common world coordinate system because their normalizations affect only the scene. Existing qualifications concerning partial visibility and numerical degree certification remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V1 refers generally to supplementary or attached code. V2 supplies an explicit repository address, implementation line ranges and the filename example_4-12.jl. These improve access and traceability without establishing changes to the implementation.

R1.justification: Six cited works are added, supporting attribution of six-point reconstruction, incidence-free three-view reconstruction and curve or oriented-feature methods. The main positioning relative to calibrated PLMP classification and previous factorization work is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include local wording edits, acknowledgement restructuring, a supplementary-material heading and insertion of Camera registration as Appendix E, moving the existing catalogue to Appendix F.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset with different typography, spacing and table rules, and many point-line diagrams are redrawn. V2 adds single-view Tables 7–8 and relocates Table 6 into the elimination discussion; the existing catalogue is redisplayed as Tables 9–12.

improvement.justification: V2 improves scope precision by explicitly separating multi-view statements from the added single-view classification. More specific code pointers and prior-work attribution also improve usability. The central classification, computational evidence and methodological limitations remain unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
